security_spec.violation_condition: In the FreeBSD kernel running in S-mode on Zicfiss hardware, code in cpu_switch (sys/riscv/riscv/swtch.S), sendsig/sigreturn (sys/riscv/riscv/exec_machdep.c), or set_mcontext/get_mcontext paths accesses the ssp CSR without first reading menvcfg to test the SSE bit. When M-mode firmware (e.g., OpenSBI) boots with menvcfg.SSE=0—globally disabling shadow stacks—the ssp access raises an illegal-instruction exception (#norm:zicfiss_m_menvcfg-sse). These kernel paths do not expect CSR-access exceptions; the unhandled trap either panics the host or silently skips save/restore, leaking or zeroing per-thread shadow stack state. In bhyve, a host that sets henvcfg.SSE=0 after this PR forces guest senvcfg.SSE to read-only zero; the simplified VU-mode check now depends solely on senvcfg.SSE (#norm:zicfiss_vu_senvcfg-sse), so guest VU-mode ssp accesses raise a virtual-instruction exception that bhyve's vmmops_exception stub (returning ENOSYS) cannot handle, corrupting guest userspace shadow stacks. Additionally, because ssp CSR access is no longer contingent on S-mode being implemented, a FreeBSD kernel that gates ssp usage on S-mode presence rather than on menvcfg.SSE will incorrectly assume availability.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: csr_read|csr_write|csr_swap inline asm referencing "ssp" in sys/riscv/riscv/swtch.S (cpu_switch), sys/riscv/riscv/exec_machdep.c (set_mcontext, get_mcontext, sendsig, sigreturn), sys/riscv/vmm/vmm_riscv.c (vmmops_vcpu_save_csrs, vmmops_vcpu_restore_csrs) without a logically-preceding CSR read of menvcfg to test SSE bit, and without a trap wrapper guarding the ssp access
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD kernel must guard every ssp CSR access with an explicit menvcfg.SSE liveness check; the menvcfg→henvcfg→senvcfg read-only-zero cascade means M-mode firmware can silently disable shadow stacks, turning ssp accesses into illegal-instruction exceptions that crash context-switch and signal-delivery paths

findings.finding: No ssp CSR access exists in cpu_switch. The function saves/restores only ra, sp, s0-s11, and conditionally FPE state. No Zicfiss/shadow-stack code is present, so the described vulnerability (accessing ssp without checking menvcfg.SSE) does not apply.
No ssp CSR access in cpu_throw. Only loads ra, sp, s0-s11 GPRs and conditionally restores FPE registers. No Zicfiss code present.
findings.snippet:
ld  ra, (PCB_RA)(x13)
ld  sp, (PCB_SP)(x13)
/* s[0-11] */
ld  s0, (PCB_S + 0 * 8)(x13)

findings.finding: No ssp CSR access in get_mcontext. Only copies GPRs (t, s, a registers, ra, sp, gp, tp, sepc, sstatus) via memcpy from trapframe and calls get_fpcontext for FPE state. No Zicfiss/shadow-stack state is captured.
No ssp CSR access in set_mcontext. Only copies GPRs back to trapframe and calls set_fpcontext. No Zicfiss state is restored.
No ssp CSR access in sendsig. Calls get_mcontext to capture state (which has no Zicfiss awareness), and writes sigframe to userspace stack. No shadow stack pointer is saved or transmitted.
No ssp CSR access in sigreturn. Copies ucontext from userspace and calls set_mcontext (which has no Zicfiss awareness). No shadow stack pointer is restored.

No ssp CSR save. Saves only: vsstatus, vsie, vstvec, vsscratch, vsepc, vscause, vstval, hvip, vsatp. Although hypcsr struct has a 'senvcfg' field, it is NOT populated in this function. No Zicfiss state is captured.
No ssp CSR restore. Restores only: vsstatus, vsie, vstvec, vsscratch, vsepc, vscause, vstval, hvip, vsatp. senvcfg is not written. No Zicfiss state is restored.

vmmops_exception is an unimplemented stub returning ENOSYS. If a guest were to trigger a virtual-instruction exception (e.g., from accessing ssp when henvcfg.SSE=0), the VMM cannot inject it into the guest and would likely VM_EXITCODE_BOGUS. However, this is a general bhyve-VMM-incompleteness issue, not Zicfiss-specific, since FreeBSD's own kernel does not use Zicfiss at all.

No MENVCFG_SSE, SENVCFG_SSE, or HENVCFG_SSE bit definitions exist. The only henvcfg bits defined are STCE, PBMTE, CBZE, CBCFE, CBIE, FIOM. No Zicfiss CSR field definitions are present anywhere in the kernel.
